rccg_open_heavens.title: HE SPEAKS PEACE II
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
message: Storms can come in various forms and with varying degrees of intensity. I recall an incident some years ago, when I was travelling from Lagos to London on a plane. When we were about to land at Heathrow Airport, the captain informed us that there was a problem with the door at the belly of the aircraft, and we all understood it to mean that the landing gear wouldn't be able to function, and in essence, the pilot was going to have to crash-land the plane. There was a storm on the plane at that moment because confusion and pandemonium broke out all around me. That day, I discovered that rich people do not want to die. I recall seeing a very wealthy man in the first-class cabin who carried a walking stick that was encrusted with diamonds at the top. Since we departed Lagos, he had been getting up, pretending to go to the toilet every now and then to show everyone his expensive walking stick. However, when he heard the captain's announcement, he really needed to use the toilet.

I tell you with confidence that even if you are anointed, you will become frightened if you are told that your plane cannot land. Therefore, I turned to God and said, "Daddy, I embarked on this journey to do Your work. You didn't tell me when I was leaving to say goodbye to my family that it would be the last time I would see them." Then He replied, saying, "Don't worry, son. I'm only delaying the plane's landing because as soon as you land, people will not let you rest, and I need to talk to you first." God's word brought peace to my heart, and the plane continued to circle around the airport while God was speaking to me. When He finished talking to me, the faulty door opened, and the plane was able to make a normal landing. Despite how tough the situation was, I was at peace because God had spoken to me.

Beloved, when you have an intimate relationship with the Prince of Peace, you will not be troubled by the things that trouble others. You will not run helter-skelter at the hint of trouble because His word will bring peace to your heart. No matter how terrible a situation may be, there is always peace to be found in God's word. Turn to His word in such instances, and it will keep your heart at peace while turning things around for the better.
prayerPoints: Reflection: Do you have an intimate relationship with the Prince of Peace?
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: When Peace Like A River Attendeth My Way

mfm_mfm.title: Jesus: The Master Over Every Storm
mfm_mfm.author: Dr. D.K. Olukoya
mfm_mfm.topic: Jesus: The Master Over Every Storm
mfm_mfm.memoryVerseText: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
message: When Jesus and His disciples were on the sea, and there was a storm, and His disciples shouted, “Master, Master, we are perishing,” I like the way Jesus rebuked them after calming the storm. What an insult! The One who, by the words of His mouth, commanded the same sea and the storm into existence, and can, by the blast of His nostrils, dry up both, was in the boat with them, and they were afraid? In the first instance, as we see in Luke 8:22, He was the One who said they should get into the boat and go over to the other side of the lake.

I have a number of questions for you to answer: Did you seek God’s face before you got into that marriage, or that business deal, or that job, or that ministry, or conceived that child? My friend, it is inevitable that there will be a few setbacks in your life because they are your stepping stones to success. Storms of life are the fire which your Creator uses to fine-tune your life and anchor you to Him, the Eternal Rock of Ages.

What then can the storm be? Is it barrenness in marriage? Is it failure in business? Is it problems in your ministry? Is it infirmity, sickness or disease? Ask Abraham, Elijah, the woman with the issue of blood, Peter, and so on. They had all been through storms, and the only thing that kept them going was their faith and obedience to God.

As in the case of the disciples on the sea, if He has led you into any situation, and a storm arises, He will never leave you nor forsake you. In fact, be of good cheer because He has overcome the world. This is why you must always carry Him along in whatever you do. In fact, NEVER enter a marriage or take any important decision in life without first knowing His will.

Beloved, do a regular audit of your heart and lifestyle to ensure that you are on course. If Jesus is asleep in the boat of your life, He says: “Peace, be still.” Also, ensure that you are always in praise mode. Then rejoice; the Lord is King.
mfm_mfm.motivationalQuote: Jehovah saw Elijah through all the threats of Jezebel. He will see you through all the rage from the pit of hell.

Any storm assigned to stop me, scatter, in the Name of Jesus.

You storm troubling my finances, peace, be still, in the Name

dclm_dclm.title: Avoid Costly Mistakes
dclm_dclm.author: Pastor W.F. Kumuyi
dclm_dclm.memoryVerseText: Therefore, O Aholibah, thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will raise up thy lovers against thee, from whom thy mind is alienated, and I will bring them against thee on every side
message: Many times, what gets people into trouble are not big but little things. They omit to do what is right. They indulge in little careless or reckless acts, including those they knew spelt disaster for other people. With the passage of time, they become self confident in their ability to tackle issues their own way. They dismiss pointers in their own lives to things that caused misfortune for others on the hollow belief that ‘it cannot happen to me’. In the process, they seal their own misfortune.

Aholibah, or Judah in Israel, had witnessed judgement that came on Samaria (or Aholah) for turning away from God and embracing the nations that did not know the Lord. They were shipped into exile. Instead of learning from God’s retribution on evil nations, Judah became more sinful before God. They connived, formed alliances with heathen nations, exposed their treasure to them and served their idols. God paid them in their own coins: He turned their new friends against them, who plundered their wealth and exposed them to shame, humiliation and disgrace.

It is only reasonable to learn from the mistakes of other people and avoid things that brought them down. Where we find that the pursuit of power, wealth and pleasure took them away from God, we must flee from such. The lives of those around us who fell out with God should be a lesson to us to shun their ways. Anything that will lull our minds and dull our sensitivity to sinful enjoyment must be avoided. We must not wait to taste the judgment of God. Anything we must do to live right before God and avoid His rod of punishment must be done now. Mercifully, God gives us grace to live the acceptable life before Him. It is thus up to us to fully tap into that inexhaustible grace and present a commendable portrait of glory and beauty, rooted in His love.
dclm_dclm.thoughtForTheDay: Sin is deceptive and deadly, and those that toy with it have bitter tales to tell.

rccg_rccg_ss_adult.assignments: List five (5) practical ways a believer can daily live a sanctified life (2×5=10 marks).
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.introduction: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.discussion:
1. THE PROCESS

A. To be sanctified

You need to see yourself as you are: filthy and in need of help
Cry to God for deliverance (Isaiah 6:5).
Present yourself to the Sanctifier – God (1 Thessalonians 5:23).
Surrender your heart to the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:2; 2 Thessalonians 2:13).
Study the word of God (John 17:17).
Soak yourself in the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 9:13-14; 1 John 1:7, 9).
Daily surrender to God (Colossians 3:6-10; Romans 6:13).
B. This process can be a painful experience, but:

The result is that you are broken and transformed into a new nature (Galatians 2:20; 2 Timothy 2:3-4).
The awareness that you do not own yourself anymore helps you prioritise God in everything you do, and whatever does not glorify Him is a no-go area for you (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
CLASS ACTIVITY 1: How do we avoid things that defile His Temple?

2. THE BENEFITS

Sanctification represents a believer’s victory over the flesh (Romans 7:24-25), the world (1 John 5:4), and the devil (James 4:7).
A sanctified believer will enjoy the ability to easily resist temptation because there is a renewed hatred for sin and lust.
Sanctification fosters intimacy with God, increases spiritual strength and stability (Psalm 15:1-5).
It also aids a ‘clean record’ for believers, that is, the enemy will not have to fool God over such (John 14:30).
It helps believers to be humble and submissive to God and to constituted authorities. The Adamic nature in man is subdued (Romans 8:1-5).
It gives the believer control over self (Galatians 2:20; Romans 6:13).
It promotes right standing before God and pure intentions of actions and words (Acts 24:16).
CLASS ACTIVITY 2: The class should discuss the ways sanctification helps a believer to live a life that honours God.
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.summary:
CONCLUSION: Sanctification is an integral part of Christian growth; every child of God must earnestly desire it.

EVALUATION: Briefly explain the process of sanctification.

CLOSING PRAYER: Father, I receive the grace to continually yield myself to your sanctification process in Jesus’ name.

christ_embassy_rhapsody.title: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.author: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome
christ_embassy_rhapsody.topic: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.memoryVerseText: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…
message: 1 Peter 1:23 tells us something remarkable; it says, “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” A similar truth is emphasized in James 1:18, “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” God’s Word gave birth to you; and what does that make you?

It means you’re the Word in flesh! The Word of God is your life-source, and every living thing must be connected to its source to live. This is why your fellowship with the Word is so important. Your true life and environment are in the Word. If you live outside the Word, you’re functioning outside your divine environment.

The Apostle Paul, by the Spirit, connects and unveils this beautifully in 2 Corinthians 3:2-3. First, he says, “Ye are our epistle…” and then he goes further to say, “…ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…” You’re the living epistle, the living message, the living expression of Christ to your world. The Lord Jesus is called the living Word; therefore, being born of His Word, you carry His life, nature, wisdom and character within you.

You’re indestructible because you’re born of His indestructible seed (His Word), which lives and abides forever. Therefore, your sufficiency, your ability, competence, strength and capacity come from your divine origin. Many struggle in life because they don’t live according to this truth. They attempt to live outside the environment of the Word.

But the Christian who meditates on the Word continually stays connected to the source of his divine nature. The more the Word dominates your spirit, the more your true nature is unveiled. God’s Word created the universe. His Word is everything. As you meditate on it, it transforms your life. Think, speak, and live the Word. Glory to God!
christ_embassy_rhapsody.confession: I’m born of God’s incorruptible Word; I’m the living epistle of Christ. My life is the manifestation of divine wisdom, glory and power. As I meditate on the Word, even now, I’m strengthened, transformed and established in victory, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

odm_odm.title: Our Daily Manna
odm_odm.author: Bishop Dr. Chris Kwakpovwe
odm_odm.memoryVerseText: When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.
odm_odm.devotionalCapsule: When God is ready to perform His wonders, protocols are suspended and mockers are silenced!
message: Beloved, our God is never late! Even when the clock of life appears to have ticked to the final second and your adversaries have already written your spiritual obituary, Jehovah El-Shaddai steps into the arena and reverses the irreversible! (Psalm 126:1).
Don't lose your joy because of temporary setbacks or stubborn delays. Delay is never denial in God's kingdom agenda. Hold on to your faith!
God is setting an ambush against your adversaries, and your mockers shall soon gather to congratulate you!
prayerPoints: O God of eleventh-hour miracles, arise and turn my captivity around this month, in Jesus' name.
Every power assigned to prolong my struggle, expire by fire, in the name of Jesus.

dunamis_seeds.title: A Heart For The Kingdom
dunamis_seeds.author: Pastor Dr. Paul Enenche
dunamis_seeds.memoryVerseText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
message: Our anchor Scripture makes it clear that your heart follows your investment. That is why you cannot claim to love the Kingdom while your resources are committed elsewhere.

The Roman centurion demonstrated this scriptural truth in Luke Chapter Seven.
Concerning him the elders of the Jews testified to Jesus, “for he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue” (Luke 7:5). You see, a heart for the Kingdom was what changed his story; it was what made Jesus to come.

Investment into the Kingdom contributes to man’s fulfilment on earth. Your seed into the Kingdom will reply to your needs when they arise. But there are people who have no seed to reply to the needs of their lives. When you are seedless, when your needs come up, nothing can help you. To be seedless is to be fruitless.

When the purpose of God does not interest you, the problems of your life will never attract Him. There are people going to church for years, yet they have never sacrificed anything for the Kingdom. When the offering basket is being passed around them, they just watch it pass by them to the next person. When it is time to build the church, to plant other churches, to send people on evangelism, to invest in television evangelism, or to even pay tithe; they look away. Yet when their problems arrive, they want God to help them. God seems to be saying: “You are not interested in Me, so I am not attracted to you. “Draw near to me, I will draw near to you” (James 4:6-7).
Don’t sit in church expecting a heavenly bank to credit you where you have made no deposit; God is your heavenly Father, not merely a source to withdraw from.

When was the last time you did something for God that touched you? Where you sow your seed will determine where you get your harvest. He that soweth to the flesh, from the flesh he will reap frustration, (Galatians 6:8) because he is spending all on what to eat, drink, wear, and drive. He that soweth to the spirit – so that churches can be built and the devil chased back to hell, will reap satisfaction. It is a matter of choice.

I came to a point in my life where I decided I would not spend anything on myself that I had not first given to God. I have been hard on myself but liberal toward the Kingdom, giving amounts I could have used to buy cars, not once, not twice. And the truth is, I do not need to spend money on hospital bills or fighting witchcraft attacks, because I have already seeded into the Kingdom, and the Kingdom attacks the need at its root.

Beloved, the Kingdom is not about what you have; it is about what you have released. Every seed planted into the things of God is a need already answered, and a battle already fought and won before it even arises.
prayerPoints: Examine what you have genuinely sacrificed for the Kingdom lately.
Correct any area of seedlessness in your life.
Choose one Kingdom project, evangelism, church building, or missions, and sow into it this week.
Draw near to God through consistent giving and service, not merely attendance.

PRAYER: Father, forgive me for every form of seedless existence. Give me a heart that is liberal toward Your Kingdom. Let my seed answer my need before it arises and let my life bring You the fulfilment You desire, Lord, in Jesus’ Name.

QUOTE: Show me a man who does not care about the cause of God on the earth, and I will show you a God who also does not care about such a man. Culled from the book 30 Secrets to the Top by Dr Paul Enenche

rccg_open_heavens.title: More Than a Conqueror
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place.
message: Life is full of battles. From the moment we are born until we leave this world, we experience different challenges. However, when a person comes to Christ, everything changes. Through Christ, the believer becomes a new creation, and the battles of life no longer have to determine the outcome. Instead of struggling without hope of victory, the believer can live with the assurance of victory in Christ.

Romans 8:37 tells believers that they are more than conquerors through Christ. A conqueror fights and defeats an enemy to obtain victory, while someone who is more than a conqueror enjoys a victory that has already been achieved. As believers, we are recipients of the victory Jesus has won.

Jesus went to the cross, defeated the devil, and secured victory for humanity. After His resurrection, He declared that all authority in heaven and on earth had been given to Him (Matthew 28:18). He then gave power to His disciples through the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:8).

When the disciples received the Holy Spirit, they began to operate in the authority Christ had given them. They cast out demons, healed the sick, preached the gospel, and continued to spread the message of Christ even when they encountered persecution. When persecution caused believers to scatter, they used the opportunity to preach the gospel in other places (Acts 8:1–4). Philip, for example, went to Samaria, where many people received the message and the city experienced great spiritual impact (Acts 8:5–8).

Being more than a conqueror does not mean that you will never face challenges. Rather, it means that when challenges arise, you can face them with the confidence that God can work through them for His purpose. What appears to be an attack can ultimately become an opportunity for God to accomplish His plan.

The death of Jesus on the cross is a powerful example. The enemy intended the crucifixion for destruction, but God used it to accomplish salvation. 1 Corinthians 2:8 explains that the rulers of that age did not understand the wisdom of God in what was taking place.
Therefore, remain confident in Christ. Trust God even when circumstances appear difficult, knowing that He can turn situations around and cause His purpose to prevail.
prayerPoints: Key Point: Being more than a conqueror means that you will always triumph over the enemy's plans.
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: Conquerors and Overcomers Now Are We

rccg_open_heavens.title: WEEP NOT
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness.
message: Sometime ago, I was praying during a programme and God said, "Open your eyes." I was almost going to say, "Lord, but I'm praying"; however, I obeyed. As I opened my eyes, I saw a woman in the congregation, her face soaked in tears, weeping as she prayed. Then, God said, "Go and tell her, 'Weep not.'" I moved towards the congregation, approached her, and tapped her as I said, "God said, 'Weep not.'" Her eyes brightened, and I returned to the altar to continue praying. A year later, that same woman stood before me, along with some other people who wanted me to pray for them. When it was her turn for me to pray for her, I greeted her and said, "Sister, how can I help you?" She opened her mouth and could only mutter, "Jesus". I asked her a second time how I could help her, and she only said, "Jesus" again. I asked her a third time, and she said the same thing. I began to get impatient because there were other people in the queue. Eventually, she got herself together, and she told me that she was the woman whom God sent me to tell not to weep the previous year. She then told me that she was crying that day because she had been married for over ten years without any children, and her husband's relatives were urging him to send her packing if she didn't give birth to any children soon. As she shared her story, I immediately understood why she found it difficult to speak at first; she was holding a baby in her right hand and another in her left. God turned her seemingly hopeless situation into an occasion for rejoicing. I pray that God will turn any seemingly hopeless situation that might exist in your life around and fill your mouth with laughter, in Jesus' name.

Beloved, if you have surrendered your life to the Lord Jesus Christ, my Daddy is saying to you today, "Weep not," just like Jesus said to the widow of Nain in today's Bible reading. Every time Jesus says, "Weep not," it is because He wants to perform a miracle. No matter how long you may have been weeping, your time of rejoicing has come. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy will surely come in the morning (Psalm 30:5). I decree that your days of rejoicing are here, in Jesus' name.
prayerPoints: Father, thank You for putting an end to my weeping and for bringing me into my days of rejoicing.
rccg_open_heavens.hymn: What A Friend We Have In Jesus

rccg_open_heavens.title: GOD OF HOPE
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
message: After Jesus died, His disciples became afraid and lost hope. John 21:3 tells us that Peter said to the other disciples, "I go a fishing." He wasn't going to fish for souls; instead, he was returning to his old job because he had lost hope. He must have thought to himself, "We thought Jesus Christ was going to rescue us from all those who are oppressing us. We thought that the age of miracles had come to stay, but now He has been crucified on a cross." When Peter told the other disciples that he was going fishing, they joined him because they had also lost hope. They felt that the best thing they could do was to return to fishing. However, Jesus appeared to them that morning as they fished and restored their hope. As they struggled to catch fish, Jesus called out to them and showed them where to cast their net. Some years ago, a young man was travelling from Kaduna, a state in Northern Nigeria, to Lagos with some other people in a vehicle. While they were on their way, they had an accident and everyone in the vehicle died except the young man. He was taken to a hospital because he was still breathing, even though he was unconscious. He was in a coma for several days, and every once in a while, he would wake up and shout, "Jesus," before returning to the coma. After a while, the doctors concluded that his case was hopeless, but they couldn't bury him because he was still breathing. Then one day, he awoke, cried out 'Jesus!', opened his eyes, and never slipped back into the coma. That young man is still alive today.

rccg_open_heavens.title: HE SPEAKS PEACE
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye

While they were scared for their lives and were trying so hard to manage the situation, Jesus was sleeping peacefully. The moment they woke Him up, He issued only one decree, "Peace, be still," and everything became calm. In the name above every other name, I decree that the peace of God that passes all understanding will rest upon you at all times, in Jesus' name.

Beloved, whenever you are in a state of confusion and chaos, cry out to God for help and listen to what He has to say to you. His Word will always bring peace and show you the way out of the situation. To receive the peace that the Prince of Peace gives, however, you must surrender your life to Him. God wants to speak peace into any troubled water that might exist in your life. To enjoy His peace, however, you must never insist on calming any storm you may be facing your own way. Surrender to God totally, and His peace shall rule every facet of your life.
prayerPoints: Key Point: God's peace rules where His way is followed and His will is done.

rccg_open_heavens.title: HE SPEAKS PEACE II
rccg_open_heavens.author: Pastor E.A. Adeboye
rccg_open_heavens.memoryVerseText: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.

When we were about to land at Heathrow Airport, the captain informed us that there was a problem with the door at the belly of the aircraft, and we all understood it to mean that the landing gear wouldn't be able to function, and in essence, the pilot was going to have to crash-land the plane. There was a storm on the plane at that moment because confusion and pandemonium broke out all around me. That day, I discovered that rich people do not want to die. I recall seeing a very wealthy man in the first-class cabin who carried a walking stick that was encrusted with diamonds at the top. Since we departed Lagos, he had been getting up, pretending to go to the toilet every now and then to show everyone his expensive walking stick. However, when he heard the captain's announcement, he really needed to use the toilet.

I tell you with confidence that even if you are anointed, you will become frightened if you are told that your plane cannot land. Therefore, I turned to God and said, "Daddy, I embarked on this journey to do Your work. You didn't tell me when I was leaving to say goodbye to my family that it would be the last time I would see them." Then He replied, saying, "Don't worry, son. I'm only delaying the plane's landing because as soon as you land, people will not let you rest, and I need to talk to you first." God's word brought peace to my heart, and the plane continued to circle around the airport while God was speaking to me. When He finished talking to me, the faulty door opened, and the plane was able to make a normal landing. Despite how tough the situation was, I was at peace because God had spoken to me.

Beloved, when you have an intimate relationship with the Prince of Peace, you will not be troubled by the things that trouble others. You will not run helter-skelter at the hint of trouble because His word will bring peace to your heart. No matter how terrible a situation may be, there is always peace to be found in God's word. Turn to His word in such instances, and it will keep your heart at peace while turning things around for the better.
prayerPoints: Reflection: Do you have an intimate relationship with the Prince of Peace?

rccg_rccg_ss_adult.assignments: List five (5) practical ways a believer can daily live a sanctified life (2×5=10 marks).
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.introduction: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.discussion:
1. THE PROCESS

A. To be sanctified

You need to see yourself as you are: filthy and in need of help
Cry to God for deliverance (Isaiah 6:5).
Present yourself to the Sanctifier – God (1 Thessalonians 5:23).
Surrender your heart to the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:2; 2 Thessalonians 2:13).
Study the word of God (John 17:17).
Soak yourself in the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 9:13-14; 1 John 1:7, 9).
Daily surrender to God (Colossians 3:6-10; Romans 6:13).
B. This process can be a painful experience, but:

The result is that you are broken and transformed into a new nature (Galatians 2:20; 2 Timothy 2:3-4).
The awareness that you do not own yourself anymore helps you prioritise God in everything you do, and whatever does not glorify Him is a no-go area for you (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
CLASS ACTIVITY 1: How do we avoid things that defile His Temple?

2. THE BENEFITS

Sanctification represents a believer’s victory over the flesh (Romans 7:24-25), the world (1 John 5:4), and the devil (James 4:7).
A sanctified believer will enjoy the ability to easily resist temptation because there is a renewed hatred for sin and lust.
Sanctification fosters intimacy with God, increases spiritual strength and stability (Psalm 15:1-5).
It also aids a ‘clean record’ for believers, that is, the enemy will not have to fool God over such (John 14:30).
It helps believers to be humble and submissive to God and to constituted authorities. The Adamic nature in man is subdued (Romans 8:1-5).
It gives the believer control over self (Galatians 2:20; Romans 6:13).
It promotes right standing before God and pure intentions of actions and words (Acts 24:16).
CLASS ACTIVITY 2: The class should discuss the ways sanctification helps a believer to live a life that honours God.
rccg_rccg_ss_adult.summary:
CONCLUSION: Sanctification is an integral part of Christian growth; every child of God must earnestly desire it.

EVALUATION: Briefly explain the process of sanctification.

CLOSING PRAYER: Father, I receive the grace to continually yield myself to your sanctification process in Jesus’ name.

dclm_dclm.title: Avoid Costly Mistakes
dclm_dclm.author: Pastor W.F. Kumuyi
dclm_dclm.memoryVerseText: Therefore, O Aholibah, thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will raise up thy lovers against thee, from whom thy mind is alienated, and I will bring them against thee on every side
message: Many times, what gets people into trouble are not big but little things. They omit to do what is right. They indulge in little careless or reckless acts, including those they knew spelt disaster for other people. With the passage of time, they become self confident in their ability to tackle issues their own way. They dismiss pointers in their own lives to things that caused misfortune for others on the hollow belief that ‘it cannot happen to me’. In the process, they seal their own misfortune.

Aholibah, or Judah in Israel, had witnessed judgement that came on Samaria (or Aholah) for turning away from God and embracing the nations that did not know the Lord. They were shipped into exile. Instead of learning from God’s retribution on evil nations, Judah became more sinful before God. They connived, formed alliances with heathen nations, exposed their treasure to them and served their idols. God paid them in their own coins: He turned their new friends against them, who plundered their wealth and exposed them to shame, humiliation and disgrace.

It is only reasonable to learn from the mistakes of other people and avoid things that brought them down. Where we find that the pursuit of power, wealth and pleasure took them away from God, we must flee from such. The lives of those around us who fell out with God should be a lesson to us to shun their ways. Anything that will lull our minds and dull our sensitivity to sinful enjoyment must be avoided. We must not wait to taste the judgment of God. Anything we must do to live right before God and avoid His rod of punishment must be done now. Mercifully, God gives us grace to live the acceptable life before Him. It is thus up to us to fully tap into that inexhaustible grace and present a commendable portrait of glory and beauty, rooted in His love.
dclm_dclm.thoughtForTheDay: Sin is deceptive and deadly, and those that toy with it have bitter tales to tell.

mfm_mfm.title: Jesus: The Master Over Every Storm
mfm_mfm.author: Dr. D.K. Olukoya
mfm_mfm.topic: Jesus: The Master Over Every Storm
mfm_mfm.memoryVerseText: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
message: When Jesus and His disciples were on the sea, and there was a storm, and His disciples shouted, “Master, Master, we are perishing,” I like the way Jesus rebuked them after calming the storm. What an insult! The One who, by the words of His mouth, commanded the same sea and the storm into existence, and can, by the blast of His nostrils, dry up both, was in the boat with them, and they were afraid? In the first instance, as we see in Luke 8:22, He was the One who said they should get into the boat and go over to the other side of the lake.

I have a number of questions for you to answer: Did you seek God’s face before you got into that marriage, or that business deal, or that job, or that ministry, or conceived that child? My friend, it is inevitable that there will be a few setbacks in your life because they are your stepping stones to success. Storms of life are the fire which your Creator uses to fine-tune your life and anchor you to Him, the Eternal Rock of Ages.

What then can the storm be? Is it barrenness in marriage? Is it failure in business? Is it problems in your ministry? Is it infirmity, sickness or disease? Ask Abraham, Elijah, the woman with the issue of blood, Peter, and so on. They had all been through storms, and the only thing that kept them going was their faith and obedience to God.

As in the case of the disciples on the sea, if He has led you into any situation, and a storm arises, He will never leave you nor forsake you. In fact, be of good cheer because He has overcome the world. This is why you must always carry Him along in whatever you do. In fact, NEVER enter a marriage or take any important decision in life without first knowing His will.

Beloved, do a regular audit of your heart and lifestyle to ensure that you are on course. If Jesus is asleep in the boat of your life, He says: “Peace, be still.” Also, ensure that you are always in praise mode. Then rejoice; the Lord is King.
mfm_mfm.motivationalQuote: Jehovah saw Elijah through all the threats of Jezebel. He will see you through all the rage from the pit of hell.

christ_embassy_rhapsody.title: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.author: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome
christ_embassy_rhapsody.topic: The Word—Your True Life And Environment
christ_embassy_rhapsody.memoryVerseText: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…
message: 1 Peter 1:23 tells us something remarkable; it says, “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” A similar truth is emphasized in James 1:18, “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” God’s Word gave birth to you; and what does that make you?

It means you’re the Word in flesh! The Word of God is your life-source, and every living thing must be connected to its source to live. This is why your fellowship with the Word is so important. Your true life and environment are in the Word. If you live outside the Word, you’re functioning outside your divine environment.

The Apostle Paul, by the Spirit, connects and unveils this beautifully in 2 Corinthians 3:2-3. First, he says, “Ye are our epistle…” and then he goes further to say, “…ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ…” You’re the living epistle, the living message, the living expression of Christ to your world. The Lord Jesus is called the living Word; therefore, being born of His Word, you carry His life, nature, wisdom and character within you.

You’re indestructible because you’re born of His indestructible seed (His Word), which lives and abides forever. Therefore, your sufficiency, your ability, competence, strength and capacity come from your divine origin. Many struggle in life because they don’t live according to this truth. They attempt to live outside the environment of the Word.

But the Christian who meditates on the Word continually stays connected to the source of his divine nature. The more the Word dominates your spirit, the more your true nature is unveiled. God’s Word created the universe. His Word is everything. As you meditate on it, it transforms your life. Think, speak, and live the Word. Glory to God!
christ_embassy_rhapsody.confession: I’m born of God’s incorruptible Word; I’m the living epistle of Christ. My life is the manifestation of divine wisdom, glory and power. As I meditate on the Word, even now, I’m strengthened, transformed and established in victory, in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

dunamis_seeds.title: A Heart For The Kingdom
dunamis_seeds.author: Pastor Dr. Paul Enenche
dunamis_seeds.memoryVerseText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
message: Our anchor Scripture makes it clear that your heart follows your investment. That is why you cannot claim to love the Kingdom while your resources are committed elsewhere.

The Roman centurion demonstrated this scriptural truth in Luke Chapter Seven.
Concerning him the elders of the Jews testified to Jesus, “for he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue” (Luke 7:5). You see, a heart for the Kingdom was what changed his story; it was what made Jesus to come.

Investment into the Kingdom contributes to man’s fulfilment on earth. Your seed into the Kingdom will reply to your needs when they arise. But there are people who have no seed to reply to the needs of their lives. When you are seedless, when your needs come up, nothing can help you. To be seedless is to be fruitless.

When the purpose of God does not interest you, the problems of your life will never attract Him. There are people going to church for years, yet they have never sacrificed anything for the Kingdom. When the offering basket is being passed around them, they just watch it pass by them to the next person. When it is time to build the church, to plant other churches, to send people on evangelism, to invest in television evangelism, or to even pay tithe; they look away. Yet when their problems arrive, they want God to help them. God seems to be saying: “You are not interested in Me, so I am not attracted to you. “Draw near to me, I will draw near to you” (James 4:6-7).
Don’t sit in church expecting a heavenly bank to credit you where you have made no deposit; God is your heavenly Father, not merely a source to withdraw from.

When was the last time you did something for God that touched you? Where you sow your seed will determine where you get your harvest. He that soweth to the flesh, from the flesh he will reap frustration, (Galatians 6:8) because he is spending all on what to eat, drink, wear, and drive. He that soweth to the spirit – so that churches can be built and the devil chased back to hell, will reap satisfaction. It is a matter of choice.

I came to a point in my life where I decided I would not spend anything on myself that I had not first given to God. I have been hard on myself but liberal toward the Kingdom, giving amounts I could have used to buy cars, not once, not twice. And the truth is, I do not need to spend money on hospital bills or fighting witchcraft attacks, because I have already seeded into the Kingdom, and the Kingdom attacks the need at its root.

Beloved, the Kingdom is not about what you have; it is about what you have released. Every seed planted into the things of God is a need already answered, and a battle already fought and won before it even arises.
prayerPoints: Examine what you have genuinely sacrificed for the Kingdom lately.
Correct any area of seedlessness in your life.
Choose one Kingdom project, evangelism, church building, or missions, and sow into it this week.
Draw near to God through consistent giving and service, not merely attendance.

PRAYER: Father, forgive me for every form of seedless existence. Give me a heart that is liberal toward Your Kingdom. Let my seed answer my need before it arises and let my life bring You the fulfilment You desire, Lord, in Jesus’ Name.

QUOTE: Show me a man who does not care about the cause of God on the earth, and I will show you a God who also does not care about such a man. Culled from the book 30 Secrets to the Top by Dr Paul Enenche
